content: Start by reading TASK.md, then complete the assignment.

content.content:
1	# Task 2: forest of 10,000 instances
2	
3	Build a scene with three.js 0.185.1 (`three` and `@types/three`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. A ground plane and exactly 10,000 scattered objects drawn with instancing (not 10,000 separate meshes): 8,000 trees (a trunk and a canopy, each instanced) and 2,000 rocks.
7	2. Placement is deterministic from a fixed seed (same forest every load), no overlaps needed.
8	3. Per-instance colour variation (canopies and rocks do not all share one colour).
9	4. One directional light that casts shadows, and exponential fog.
10	5. The camera slowly orbits the forest and the whole scene is visible.
11	
12	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
13	
14	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
15	
16	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
17	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
18	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
19	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
20	- When you are done, call `finish`.
21

content.thinking:
I'm planning the scene setup with a disc-shaped ground and light exponential fog for visibility, then building instanced trees with varied trunk and canopy colors plus scattered rocks with scale variation for natural randomness.

Now I'm adding directional lighting with shadows sized to cover the whole area, a seeded random generator for consistent placement, and tuning the camera distance and field of view to frame the forest nicely before finalizing the canvas size and pixel ratio.
Checking visibility against the forest's extent and camera distance, the fog at 0.006 density is a bit too heavy at that range, so I'll lower it to 0.004 to keep things visible.

input.summary: Wrote src/main.ts. It draws a ground plane and 10,000 instanced objects: 8,000 trees (an instanced trunk mesh and an instanced canopy mesh) and 2,000 instanced rocks. Placement comes from a seeded mulberry32 generator, so the forest is the same on every load. Canopies, trunks and rocks get per-instance colours through setColorAt. One shadow-casting directional light and FogExp2 are set up. The camera orbits slowly at radius 125 and height 70, looking at the origin, so the whole 120x120 forest stays in view. The loop runs on requestAnimationFrame and sets window.__EVAL_READY__ after the first frame. Typecheck passed. I did not run `vite build` or view the render in a browser. I lowered the fog density from 0.006 to 0.004 after the typecheck and did not re-run it.
